content.title: About
content.content: Stewed potatoes are a dish made from diced potatoes slowly cooked in broth or sauce together with vegetables, spices, and sometimes meat. The potatoes keep their shape while absorbing a tender, flavorful taste from the long simmering.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stewing retains more vitamins and minerals compared with boiling.
In traditional Russian cuisine, stewed potatoes are often cooked with carrots, onions, and bay leaf.
Some regions add tomato paste or cream for a richer flavor.
Stewed potatoes are frequently used as a base for casseroles and ragouts.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, the dish can last 3‑4 days.

items.title: Rich source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Stewing preserves part of the vitamin C, important for immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The fiber in potatoes aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Stewed potatoes deliver slow‑releasing energy, helpful for maintaining stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Beta‑carotene (in colored varieties)
items.content: Orange and yellow potatoes contain provitamin A, supporting vision and skin health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Excessive salt addition can increase hypertension risk; control the amount of salt used.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Solanine presence
items.content: Green spots and sprouts contain solanine—a toxin that should be removed before cooking.

items.title: Nightshade allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed potatoes can be served as a main dish, a side to meat or fish, incorporated into salads, casseroles, and soups. Reheat in the microwave or skillet, adding fresh herbs for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months; thaw and reheat before serving.
